verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 5.5 'Order and truncation of a search': 'The cap acts when the search is about to add one position more than the cap: it stops at once with truncated true and exactly cap items' (unlabelled, no qualifier). This supports the finding's expected. Oracle lie_games.orbit_graph_capped(C, seeds, mutate, cap) on seeds times 2^60 gives truncated False at cap equal to the orbit size.
verdicts.evidence: I read everything at b9b8504 (the worktree is detached there and clean). SPEC 5.5 has no 'may', no [D] mark and no clause that limits the rule to some arithmetic. E-2 puts every non-finite and custom board on Big because entries pass 2^53, so values beyond 2^53 are a specified case. search.ts:289-298: on a SafeInt or Big board, orbitGraph first runs searchOnNumbers. Its doc comment says a seed that is not a safe integer 'hands over at once'. Lines 300-320 are the generic loop, and line 320 returns truncated false. F3 (read as text from worktree-agent-a19febfb0f4c5a241:redteam/rt11-p4/mutants/F3-generic-M14.patch) changes that line to truncated: items.length >= cap. That is not an equivalent mutant (RT-11 section 6), because the generic loop can end naturally with exactly cap items. Oracle, run with python3 -I on copies of reference/ from b9b8504, using positions: L.orbit_graph_capped(L.cartan('A',2), units times 2^60, L.mutate, 6) gives 6 items, truncated False, complete_layers 2 (cap 5 gives True). B2 at cap 8, G2 at cap 12 and A3 at cap 12 all give False. The triangle [[2,-1,-1],[-1,2,-1],[-1,-1,2]] from [2^60,0,0] gives False at maxDepth 3, 6 and 10 with cap 18, 39 and 63. So the oracle backs the finding's expected and contradicts the mutant. mainthread-fast-paths.test.ts:330-355 (// regression: P3-RT-07-02) has these handover cases: [[2,-4],[-4,2]] and the others at cap 2000 with maxDepth 60; A2 with seeds [2^60,-2^59] and [1,0] at cap 50, which has at most 12 items; and the 12-cycle cases, which are on the fast path. None ends with exactly cap items. The other cap-boundary tests (p1-search 'triangle with a cap of 9', p3a-orbit-size) use small values, so they run the fast path. decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md item (4) records the two loops and claims equivalence on 'values past 2^53', but records no exemption for the cap boundary. gate-G4.md (4e3e839, which names b9b8504) has no open item on this, and nothing in round1-deferred.json or the P4 'known and decided' list covers it.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 5.5 has no permitting clause for any arithmetic; R2 failed, because the finding reads 5.5 correctly and an exact-cap natural end is not truncated; R3 failed, because orbitGraph is phase 1 and E-2's Big boards exist at G4; R4 failed, because the oracle gives truncated False at cap equal to the orbit size on seeds times 2^60 (A2 cap 6, triangle maxDepth 3 cap 18), so it backs the expected and not the mutant; R5 failed, because 5.5 is not [D] and the residual-perf fragment records no exemption; R6 failed, because there is no open record and the P3-RT-07-02 regression test never ends a handover search at exactly cap; the major level matches RT-11 attack 31 (a surviving M14 is major) and round 1's handling of surviving mutants.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.6 [D] 'Main-thread work': 'its worst case, 2000 positions on a board with 12 nodes in `Big` arithmetic, took 9 ms in the measurement of section 5.5. A Vitest benchmark repeats that case (the 12-cycle with one chord, joining nodes 1 and 7, as in reference/bench_orbit.mjs) and fails above 25 ms (median of seven runs).' SPEC 5.5 says the 9 ms came from 'a direct implementation' with decimal-text keys. CONTRACTS.md 3 says '2000 positions, Big'. decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md item (4) and the 'MERGE: red-team round 1, residual fixes' entry record the engine change but not the benchmark.
verdicts.evidence: I read these at b9b8504. orbit.bench.ts asserts board.arith toBe Big, seeds the 12 bigint unit vectors on the 12-cycle with the 1-7 chord, and uses cap 2000, maxDepth 40, 7 runs, the median and 25 ms. So its inputs match 7.6 and CONTRACTS 3 word for word. search.ts:291-293 sends every Big board to searchOnNumbers while values are safe, so the timed call no longer does bigint arithmetic with decimal keys. reference/bench_orbit.mjs, the measurement 7.6 names, runs its 'Big' case through a bigint object with decimal-text keys. F9 (read as text) slows only lines 300-317, which these seeds never reach. Records: decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md (4) says 'orbitGraph on a SafeInt or Big board searches on plain numbers while every value is a safe integer', with 'Default used: none' and 'Reason: SPEC 7.6 and E-9'. It never names orbit.bench.ts or what the benchmark now times, and no other entry of that fragment does either. The DECISIONS.md MERGE entry for the round 1 residual fixes says 'orbitGraph on plain numbers with the bigint path from the same move; no result, cap or interface changed' and is also silent on the benchmark. The only other benchmark records are the P3 stage 3.1 MERGE entry (medians 19.75 and 21.60 ms, the bigint loop), the P4-A1 and P4 merge records of the medians, and the GATE G4 entry (median 12.61 ms). None records a change of the arithmetic measured. Nothing in the P4 'known and decided' list covers it. Possible counter-reading: E-2 says 'A board carries its arithmetic', and its [D] sentence 'writing the half-dozen core functions twice is acceptable; the tests do not care' would let 'in Big arithmetic' name the board, which the benchmark satisfies. But 7.6 and 5.5 tie 'that case' to bigint computation, so the text is ambiguous and nothing in it permits the benchmark to stop timing Big arithmetic. Phase: the benchmark is phase 3 (CONTRACTS 3, P3-A2), at or below G4.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 7.6 permits no other arithmetic for the benchmark and the 25 ms bound being met is not the claim; R2 is only partial, because the inputs, board arithmetic, cap, runs and threshold match 7.6 and CONTRACTS 3 literally, but whether 'in Big arithmetic' names the board (E-2) or the timed computation (5.5, bench_orbit.mjs) is an ambiguity for the owner, not a permission; R3 failed, because the benchmark is phase 3 at gate G4; R4 does not apply to a timing; R5 failed, because the 7.6 [D] text itself says Big and the residual-perf fragment (item 4) and the residual MERGE entry record the engine change but never what the benchmark now measures, so the finding's 'no record' part holds; R6 failed, because there is no open item in gate-G4.md or round 1; if true the claim falls under major ('a behaviour the specification states is missing or wrong', or a missing required record).

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 7.5 A-3 (unlabelled; the 7.5 heading has no [D]): 'Each node button has a name and state built from a fixed template: ... "City 2, population 1, mutation would raise it".' CONTRACTS.md 5.3 repeats it as an exact string. RT-11 attack 33 says 'a loose comparison of a fixed sentence (minor per file)'. The passage supports the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: I read these at b9b8504. site/tests/e2e/T15.spec.ts:132, inside the loop over the square's four buttons in the test 'frozen population: every city is happy and a Martian wakes the board', is: expect(await b.getAttribute('aria-label')).toMatch(/^City \d, population 1, mutation would change nothing$/). The only exact aria-label in the file is T15.spec.ts:236, 'Node 1, value 1, cannot be fired', which is a Node name and not a City name. site/tests/unit/tools/T15.test.ts:580 checks only endsWith('mutation would change nothing'). T15 is phase 2 ('### T15. Affine Playground (phase 2)'), at or below G4. The fixes for P3-RT-11-08 covered A-4 sentences in T01, T05, T07 and T15. decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-tools.md 'whole sentences in T10's and T11's live-region checks (sibling of P3-RT-11-08)' covers only T10 and T11. In round 1 the P3-RT-11-08 reproduce verifier saw this line (then T15.spec.ts:120) only as an extra grep line 'that the finding does not claim'. It is not an open or deferred item: there is no match in round1-deferred.json or RESULTS.md, gate-G4.md has no open item on it, and the P4 'known and decided' list does not name it. No decisions fragment allows a regular-expression comparison of an A-3 name.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because A-3 fixes the template, which includes the city label, with no qualifier; R2 failed, because the regex leaves the label free and ties it to no data-node, as the finding says; R3 failed, because T15 is phase 2 at G4; R4 does not apply; R5 failed, because 7.5 A-3 is not [D] and nothing records a loose comparison; R6 failed, because round 1 saw the line only in a verifier's evidence and never recorded it as an open item; minor is the rubric's level for a test that could be stronger without being wrong (RT-11 attack 33).
